summary.prose: Building this fix means changing one decision in the TypeScript reader's call walk so a built-in method name drops a call only when its receiver is not known to be user code: first the shapes that need no types (bare calls, this/super, imports), then receivers proven by a type annotation or a new expression on fields, parameters and locals, and finally proving the restored calls resolve correctly and show up on the installed daemon after a re-index.

tasks.title: Bare, this/super and import-bound calls are kept whatever the name
tasks.summary: In src/indexer/parser/typescript.ts, collect the file's import-bound local names per parse (default, namespace, named, aliased) and change the walkForCalls filter: BUILTIN_METHODS no longer applies to bare calls or to member calls on this, super or an import-bound identifier; BUILTIN_OBJECTS still applies. The import bindings form the outermost receiver scope so a nearer local or parameter declaration shadows them. Add reader unit tests.
acceptanceChecks: A bare call to parse/find/create records a CALLS row; bare setTimeout/require record none
Calls on default, namespace, named and aliased import bindings record rows; a local that shadows an import name does not
Built-in-named member calls on untyped locals and built-in object receivers record no row
Import bindings of one file do not apply to the next file parsed

tests.name: S001 t1: bare calls to user functions named like built-ins are kept; bare global functions are not
S001 t1: calls on this, super and import bindings are kept whatever the name; a local shadowing an import is not
S001 t1: built-in-named member calls on untyped locals and built-in objects record no row, and import bindings do not leak to the next file

tasks.title: Typed and new-created fields, parameters and locals prove a user receiver
tasks.summary: In the reader, collect per class the this.<field> names whose field or constructor parameter property is typed with a non-built-in class, initialised with new X() of one, or assigned this.<field> = new X(); and per scope (the existing frame) the parameters and locals declared that way. A fixed built-in class list, unions, arrays, primitives and function types never prove a user object. Member calls on proven receivers are kept whatever the name. Add reader unit tests.
acceptanceChecks: this.store.find() is kept for a typed field, a constructor parameter property, a new-initialised field and a this.store = new Store() assignment
repo.find() is kept for a typed parameter and for a new-initialised local
Receivers typed Promise/Map/EventEmitter/Item[]/Array<Item>/a union, or untyped, record no row for built-in method names
Class field proofs do not leak to another class or the next file
In a .js file, a call on a new-initialised local is kept and one on an untyped local is dropped

tests.name: S001 t2: calls on typed, new-initialised and constructor-assigned fields are kept whatever the name
S001 t2: calls on typed parameters and new-initialised locals are kept; built-in, array, union and untyped receivers are not
S001 t2: field proofs do not leak across classes or files, and JavaScript follows the same rules

tasks.title: Resolution integration, installed-daemon smoke and the full sweep
tasks.summary: Over a temporary store and real files, the restored calls resolve to the user definitions (bare imported parse, this-call, field call, namespace-import call) and items.find() beside a same-file function find creates no edge. After the push, on the installed daemon, a small TypeScript repository shows callers of a built-in-named user function after index and after repo.reindex. Then run the full sweep per directory.
acceptanceChecks: The integration test shows each restored call resolved and no edge from items.find() to the user find
Smoke evidence file: callers appear after index and after repo.reindex on the installed daemon
Full sweep recorded with every failure classified

S001 t3: the installed daemon shows callers of a built-in-named function after index and repo.reindex
